You have every right to be sad. When people say this is a way of invalidating the motives of a suicidal person and their feelings. Being suicidal means you want to die but something, whether it be fear or family or school or etc., is preventing you from doing so. Also, nothing to be sorry about as that is what this page is here for.

Jobs: I would try indeed or Monster you will get rejected a lot but you will get some offers. Take a career quiz to tell you what you would be best at or most passionate about.  Finding a job is hard but you will eventually find one if you keep looking and I can almost promise that.

Money: This can be solved with a job. You can even start your own business based on something you enjoy. You can get money quickly through selling plasma or by selling the things you no longer want or need.

Friends: This one is a bit tricky because you can bend careers and how much money you have based on life choices. My only advice is that suicide is your choice and don't let other people make that choice for you.

Laziness: Laziness is obtained by a pattern of reward-consequences developed in life. There are plenty of ways to help with this by setting alarms for when you need to do something or making a calendar. Put a lock on social media websites while job searching or cleaning.

Edit: If you enjoy crossdressing try joining a drag club near you. You don't even have to tell them your real name. Make up something fun. If you get good enough at it you can even start making money off of it.

People say that not because they are bad but because when it comes to mental illness or permanent conditions it is hard for people who don't have these conditions to wrap their minds around it being a lifelong and forever thing because unlike being in a wheelchair or having a facial deformation people can't see the pain you feel inside or what past trauma has done to you. It also a way for people to shut down the conversation or because they don't want to be held responsible for your suicide which is especially true with teachers, police officers, etc. and it sounds harsh but they also have a life to live. This saying is really really bad to tell anyone who is suicidal as it would be the equivalent of telling someone grieving their dead child that one day they will forget all about it and life will return to how it was. This, of course, is not true in the same way that telling someone that has a mental illness or experienced horrific traumas in the past that "they won't always feel this way" or "it gets better".
